packages.title: DfT domestic transport NOx 29 percent QA
facts: DfT reports domestic transport accounted for 29% of domestic nitrogen oxides emissions in 2024.
NOx is an air pollutant metric rather than greenhouse-gas CO2e.
The 29% denominator is domestic NOx emissions.
Air-pollutant shares must not be merged with the 30% GHG share.
No parcel NOx value is inferred.

packages.title: DfT domestic transport PM2.5 26 percent QA
facts: DfT reports domestic transport accounted for 26% of domestic PM2.5 emissions in 2024.
PM2.5 is particulate matter under 2.5 micrometres aerodynamic diameter.
This share concerns emissions of an air pollutant rather than ambient concentration.
The statistic is not a greenhouse-gas percentage.
No parcel PM2.5 emissions are inferred.

packages.title: DfT domestic transport PM10 22 percent QA
facts: DfT reports domestic transport accounted for 22% of domestic PM10 emissions in 2024.
PM10 and PM2.5 are distinct particulate-matter metrics.
The transport PM10 share is not interchangeable with the transport GHG share.
The published domestic scope must be retained.
No parcel PM10 value is inferred.

packages.title: DfT domestic-transport scope QA
facts: The DfT 2024 release distinguishes domestic transport environmental impacts.
Domestic scope must not be silently expanded to international transport.
Greenhouse-gas and air-pollutant results use different measures.
Mode or activity statistics are not automatically emissions totals.
No local property emissions are inferred from the national release.

packages.title: ONS direct energy use 165.4 Mtoe QA
facts: ONS estimates UK direct energy use at 165.4 million tonnes of oil equivalent in 2024.
Mtoe is an energy unit rather than a greenhouse-gas unit.
The residence-account environmental accounts provide the energy context.
Energy use and emissions must remain separate measures.
No parcel energy consumption is inferred.

packages.title: ONS fossil direct-energy share 77.7 percent QA
facts: ONS reports fossil fuels accounted for 77.7% of UK direct energy use in 2024.
The percentage is an energy-source share, not an emissions share.
Fossil energy includes multiple fuel types.
The 2024 reference year must be preserved.
No parcel fuel mix is inferred.

packages.title: ONS renewable direct-energy share 15.3 percent QA
facts: ONS reports renewable energy accounted for 15.3% of UK direct energy use in 2024.
Renewable energy share is distinct from renewable electricity generation share.
The denominator is direct energy use in the environmental accounts.
The measure is not avoided-emissions evidence.
No parcel renewable share is inferred.

packages.title: ONS natural-gas fossil-fuel share QA
facts: ONS reports natural gas was the largest single fossil-fuel source in 2024.
Natural gas accounted for 45.2% of fossil-fuel use in the environmental accounts context.
This percentage is within fossil-fuel use rather than total GHG emissions.
Fuel-use shares must preserve their denominator.
No parcel gas-consumption share is inferred.

packages.title: ONS wind wave tidal renewable share QA
facts: ONS reports wind, wave and tidal energy was the largest renewable-energy source in 2024.
It accounted for 28.4% of renewable energy use in the environmental accounts.
This share is within renewable energy rather than total direct energy.
Renewable-source share is not a greenhouse-gas total.
No parcel generation mix is inferred.

packages.title: ONS energy-by-industry source fuel QA
facts: ONS publishes energy use by industry, source and fuel for 1990 to 2024.
The dataset distinguishes around 130 industry groups, multiple source categories and fuel categories.
Energy activity data are not equivalent to industry greenhouse-gas emissions.
Industry classifications and fuel labels must be preserved.
No parcel value is inferred from an industry table.

packages.title: ONS fossil-fuel table exclusion QA
facts: ONS fossil-fuel-by-type data cover coal, natural gas, petrol, road diesel, fuel oil, gas oil, aviation fuel and other fossil categories.
The table explicitly excludes biofuels and waste.
Excluded categories must not be silently added to fossil totals.
Fuel-use data are energy activity rather than CO2e.
No parcel fuel use is inferred.

packages.title: ONS renewable and waste energy dataset QA
facts: ONS publishes renewable and waste energy use by source and industry from 1990 to 2024.
The dataset includes multiple renewable sources rather than one combined technology.
Renewable and waste energy use must remain distinct from fossil-fuel tables.
Energy-use statistics are not direct emissions measurements.
No parcel renewable use is inferred.

packages.title: ONS renewable-heat technology QA
facts: ONS renewable-heat energy data include active solar heating, heat pumps and geothermal aquifers.
The dataset covers 1990 to 2024.
Heat-generation energy is not the same as installed-device count.
Renewable heat does not by itself quantify avoided emissions.
No parcel heat output is inferred.

packages.title: ONS environmental-accounts revision QA
facts: ONS environmental-account datasets state that estimates may be revised when further data become available.
Revisions may also occur when methods or systems change.
Scheduled revisions are distinct from corrections of errors.
Dataset vintage must be preserved for reproducibility.
No superseded figure is silently presented as current.

packages.title: ONS Environmental Accounts to DUKES bridge QA
facts: The 2026 Environmental Accounts release includes an energy-use bridging table connecting Environmental Accounts and DUKES concepts.
A bridge exists because accounting treatments can differ between statistical systems.
Values should not be assumed identical without the bridge methodology.
Energy-accounting alignment is separate from greenhouse-gas accounting basis.
No parcel inference is made from the national bridge.

packages.title: DUKES 2025 future-release guard QA
facts: The Digest of UK Energy Statistics 2025 release is confirmed for 30 July 2026.
At 25 July 2026 that release is still in the future.
The announcement describes comprehensive annual production, trade and consumption statistics.
A release announcement is not observed data from the future edition.
No 2025 DUKES values are fabricated.

packages.title: UK Energy in Brief 2025 future-release guard QA
facts: UK Energy in Brief 2025 is confirmed for release on 30 July 2026.
At 25 July 2026 the edition has not yet been released.
Its scope includes energy production, use, greenhouse-gas context, renewables, efficiency, prices and fuel poverty.
The announcement must not be treated as the released statistical contents.
No future value is used.

packages.title: Renewables Obligation three-month lag QA
facts: DESNZ states Renewables Obligation certificate and generation data are three months in arrears.
The relevant tables are updated monthly.
Publication month is therefore not the same as generation month.
Lag must be retained when aligning with other energy datasets.
No current-month generation is inferred from a lagged certificate table.

packages.title: RO certificate generation emissions separation QA
facts: Energy Trends renewables tables include certificates and generation associated with the Renewables Obligation.
A certificate count is not an electricity-generation quantity.
Electricity generation is not itself a greenhouse-gas emissions total.
Capacity, generation and certificates must remain separate metrics.
No parcel emissions are inferred from certificate issuance.

packages.title: Domestic RHI scheme-year 12 QA
facts: Ofgem's Domestic RHI annual report published 17 July 2026 covers Scheme Year 12.
The reporting period is 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026.
The report concerns scheme activity rather than a national greenhouse-gas inventory.
Financial-year style scheme periods must not be relabelled calendar years.
No parcel emissions are inferred from scheme participation.
